title: Pronouns, time words and place words
intro: Read this before the questions. The reporter looks at the sentence from a different person, time and place, so the words that point to them change.

blocks.title: personal and possessive pronouns
items: Pronouns follow the **speaker** and the **listener**, as seen by the reporter: 'I like **my** job,' said Tom. → Tom said **he** liked **his** job.
**I → he / she**, **me → him / her**, **my → his / her**, **mine → his / hers**.
**you** depends on who is listening: 'You are late,' Tom said to Ann. → Tom told Ann **she** was late. If the reporter is the listener, you becomes **I**: Tom told me **I** was late.
If the reporter is the speaker, nothing changes: 'I like my job,' said Tom. → (Tom, later) I said **I** liked **my** job.

blocks.title: demonstratives and place words
items: **this → that**: 'I like this book.' → She said she liked **that** book.
**come → go** and **bring → take** when the movement is now away from the reporter.
**Relative pronouns** (who, which, that, whose) do **not** change: 'The man who called is here.' → She said the man **who** had called was there.

blocks.title: time words
items: **now → then** (or at that moment); **today → that day**; **tonight → that night**.
**yesterday → the day before** (the previous day); **tomorrow → the next day** (the following day).
**last week → the week before** (the previous week); **next week → the following week** (the week after).
**the day before yesterday → two days before**; **the day after tomorrow → in two days' time** (or two days later).

blocks.title: when nothing changes
items: If you report **at the same time and in the same place**, the time and place words can stay: 'I'll do it **today**,' she said. → (the same day) She said she'd do it **today**.
Never mix the two worlds: *She said she would come tomorrow* is wrong if the report is made later. Use **the next day**.
